items.title: Walter "Furry" Lewis Interview, 1968-09-02
items.q: So I played with Anderson and this captain, John Handy. ... I worked with all them years ago.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, yeah, he was. He was versatile, too, man. Yeah. He could play anything, you know. That's what made the guys pretty popular, because they, they were versatile. They could play anything, you see? A lot of time, uh, I think a lot of those guys, they'd give them one category, and they'd play one or two blues, and that was it. That's where they could go. Yeah. Well, a lot of people would like the way they'd sing it, so they'd get them just to, just to hear that one particular blues. Yeah. But after that,…
Well, with John's motto, you know.

And always something you can learn. I don't care how old you get or how much you can play, man, it's something come out of every—a musician never learns. He's never educated because there's something coming out every day he got to learn. And I always was taught that education is not what you know already. Yeah, I know. They smoke up on what you have not learned. Yeah. And that's true. Yeah.
